newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans small Finnish Gulf coal export outlet.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans small Finnish Gulf coal export outlet.

text.p: Russia plans to build a new coal export outlet on the Finnish Gulf near St Petersburg as part of a government plan to increase the area's export capacity, Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Lobov said.
Lobov, speaking at a ceremony at the weekend to launch the project, said the facility, at Ust Luga, would have an annual capacity of eight million tonnes when completed by 1999.
The project is part of a proposal to build a giant export terminal for dry goods at Ust Luga that would handle a total of 35 million tonnes a year.
Rosugol, the state coal mining monopoly, and unnamed foreign lending institutions will finance the $166 million dollar coal outlet, to be built by Rosugol subsidiary Rosterminalugol.

Rosugol chief executive officer Yuri Malyshev said the federal government had earmarked 2.5 trillion roubles to restructure Russia's inefficient coal industry next year and that some of the money would be used to build the port.

Ilya Baskin, chief executive officer of AO Ust Luga, the company that will help manage the facility, said Belgian, German and Dutch banks were interested in financing the project, but he gave no further details.
